key_insight: A modified Gram-based dynamic mixed SGS framework lets researchers tune the balance between structural accuracy and dissipative regularization, with sequential coupling giving the best overall tradeoff.
engineering_relevance: For LES of geophysical turbulence, the new closure design can improve robustness by preserving backscatter fidelity while avoiding the noisy, under-dissipative behavior of purely structurally dominated models.
method: Developed a parametric family of dynamic mixed models: fully-coupled, sequential, and fully-decoupled.
Used Gram-based least-squares estimation to control the balance between functional eddy viscosity and structural closure terms.
Tested with the Leith model and fourth-order nonlinear gradient model in forced 2D and beta-plane turbulence.
evidence_signal: A priori tests matched ideal SGS forcing and local energy exchange, while a posteriori runs showed the sequential DMM improved vorticity fields, spectra, and domain-averaged diagnostics relative to structurally dominated variants.
watch_item: Models weighted too strongly toward the structural term can reproduce backscatter well but may produce high-wavenumber noise and insufficient net dissipation in long runs.
paper_title: Modified Dynamic Mixed Subgrid-scale Models for Geophysical Flows: Forced Two-Dimensional and $β$-plane Turbulence
